item.title: EU economy beats expectations but energy shock keeps inflation higher for longer
item.description: The EU economy is set to grow by 1.4% this year, faster than expected in the spring, but inflation will stay above 3% this year and next as the Iran war keeps energy prices high, the European Commission said in its autumn forecast on Tuesday.

item.title: Neanderthal gene variant linked to lower schizophrenia risk, study finds
item.description: Modern humans have Neanderthals to thank for a common genetic variant that affects the occipital lobe.

item.title: Germany and Norway to buy more US air defences for Ukraine, including Patriot missiles
item.description: Ukraine has desperately been urging its backers to help find more Patriots as they are the only system capable of shooting down Russian ballistic missiles.

item.title: Kim Jong Un tours ski resort with wife and daughter
item.description: North Korea's Kim Jong Un tours a ski resort in Samjiyon with his family, smiling and smoking in photos.

item.title: What to watch in Nvidia’s first earnings report since Huang’s resignation
item.description: AI chip giant Nvidia reports its first earnings on Tuesday since a spy scandal forced co-founder Jensen Huang to quit. Investors will scrutinise what the chipmaker says about its future and whether its customers will keep spending heavily on AI data centres.

item.title: France and Malaysia agree rare earths deal as Macron looks beyond China for supplies
item.description: Kuala Lumpur is making an exception to its ban on exporting raw minerals for Paris, as the two countries raise relations to a strategic partnership.

item.title: Iran claims drone attack on US radar system at Sheikh Isa air base in Bahrain
item.description: Bahrain was heavily targeted earlier in the war, which started in February, but had been peaceful for weeks until an Iranian drone attack on Friday. A second followed on Sunday.

item.title: From exercise to intermittent fasting: What does science say about boosting brain health?
item.description: Researchers are exploring how lifestyle choices affect the ageing brain.

item.title: Council of Europe chief Berset warns against sidelining human rights in migration crackdown
item.description: Speaking to Euronews, Council of Europe Secretary General Alain Berset defended governments’ right to tighten migration policies but insisted they must honour their human rights commitments, as five EU countries unveiled plans for a return hub in Rwanda.

item.title: Polish man loses hair and ability to sweat after red ink tattoo, undergoes 8 surgeries
item.description: A 36-year-old man in Poland experienced rare, debilitating complications after a tattoo done with red ink.

item.title: Video shows Pope Leo XIV struck in the face by rosary bracelet
item.description: Pope Leo XIV was struck in the face by a rosary bracelet thrown from the crowd in Lima before brushing it off and blessing a baby.

item.title: China says it has 'no information' on whether North Korea's leader Kim will meet Trump
item.description: Trump and Kim met in Singapore in June 2018, then in Hanoi in February 2019 and at the Demilitarised Zone in North Korea in June 2019.

item.title: Melbourne Cup runner So You Are found dumped in Sydney rubbish bin
item.description: The gelding, who had won over €800,000 in prize money, was put down after a severe bout of colic, and his trainer wants a full explanation.

item.title: Denmark hosts Tetris showdown as Dutch champion takes victory
item.description: Over 40 gamers compete at Denmark's European Tetris championship, where Dutch player Eve Commandeur defeats British rival Sam Vaughn in the final.

item.title: Exploring Türkiye’s artisanal heritage through its cities
item.description: From carpet-weaving and pottery-making to metalwork and paper marbling, Türkiye has a rich history of craftsmanship. Different regions boast different skills, and a tour of the country reveals some of its most treasured cultural pastimes.

item.title: 'Hero of mine': Sam Altman praises Nvidia's Jensen Huang
item.description: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman has praised Nvidia boss Jensen Huang for his contribution to the artificial intelligence revolution. Speaking at a conference in Menlo Park, California, Altman said it was difficult to imagine the industry's growth without Huang and the company he built.

item.title: Australia eases backpacker visa cuts after backlash from regional employers
item.description: Proposed cuts to tens of thousands of visas prompted a backlash from rural employers that rely on backpackers on farms for fruit picking, and for restaurant and tourism jobs.

item.title: 53-fingered robot pianist and human musician perform Chopin together
item.description: In Italy, 53-fingered robot pianist TeoTronico takes on Roberto Prosseda, raising questions about whether machines can truly express emotion through music.

item.title: Robert Pattinson as James Bond: Inspired casting coup or risk-averse choice?
item.description: Verdict: In choosing Robert Pattinson as the new James Bond, has Amazon made an inspired casting choice or taken the safe bet?

item.title: Measles in Europe: Which countries have the most cases this year?
item.description: Measles cases are falling in Europe, but there are exceptions.

item.title: Police raid Turkish pro-opposition broadcaster Sözcü TV, carry out arrests
item.description: It was the latest move against pro-opposition media, coming a month after police raided Turkey's most-watched news channel, Halk TV, where they shut down broadcasts and installed an administrator.

item.title: Nvidia board not considering bringing Jensen Huang back as CEO as Trump backs return, reports
item.description: It comes as US President Donald Trump said he “wouldn’t mind” seeing Jensen Huang reinstated as Nvidia CEO.

item.title: Europe’s Sisyphean task: Staying ahead of Moscow's menace
item.description: Good morning. It’s Tuesday and my name is Angela Skujins. On today’s agenda: Defence ministers descend on Brussels to discuss hybrid threats and the China challenge, while the migration debate enters its second day from ice-cold Vienna.

item.title: ‘Everest of diving’: Underwater adventures in Kea exploring Titanic's sister ship Britannic
item.description: Off the coast of Kea lie three famous shipwrecks that attract sea lovers worldwide. The Greek island also offers about 81 kilometres of hiking paths in 12 main routes.

item.title: Portugal plans support for vulnerable families and microenterprises to buy electric cars
item.description: Will subsidies for buying electric cars make mobility more sustainable in Portugal? The measure aims to help vulnerable families but raises doubts about running costs, reliance on private cars and EU policy towards Chinese competition.

item.title: 72 hours without help: How the EU wants Europeans to prepare for a crisis
item.description: Europe urges households to be self-sufficient for at least the first three days of a crisis. Citizens should have enough food, water, and medicine, keep evacuation bags ready, and have emergency plans to face natural and human-induced disasters.

item.title: UK leader Andy Burnham says Brexit hasn't worked ahead of reset summit with EU
item.description: Burnham argued that the promise of the pro-Brexit campaign that Britain would "take back control" of its borders, laws and economy had not been delivered.

item.title: Europe Today: Rwanda migrant hub, Crimea bridge strike, Iran's Hormuz offer
item.description: Five EU countries have struck a deal with Rwanda to host the first return hub for migrants outside the bloc, and we're live from the Vienna Migration Conference. Also: another attack on the Crimean Bridge, new EU sanctions on Russia, US-Iran tensions and the Commission's economic forecast.

item.title: Turning Italian? Why Italy is the G7's unlikely fiscal role model
item.description: HSBC says every G7 member will need Italian-style primary surpluses to stabilise debt, as Rome borrows more cheaply than Paris ahead of an election-year budget.

item.title: Japan scrambles jets after suspected Russian planes enter airspace, Tokyo says
item.description: Tokyo's announcement came hours after South Korea said it had deployed fighter jets and conducted tactical manoeuvres after several Russian military aircraft entered its air defence zone.

item.title: Avocados grow where olive trees once stood: Italian farms ravaged by disease turn a profit
item.description: In Puglia, Xylella fastidiosa has killed a third of the region’s 60 million olive trees – which once produced almost half of Italy’s olive oil.

item.title: Russia to hold emergency talks after Crimea bridge attack causes section to collapse
item.description: The 19-kilometre bridge connects Krasnodar Krai in Russia with the Crimean peninsula across the Kerch Strait and was built by Moscow following the 2014 occupation.

item.title: Heatwaves are the worst weather for our health and the economy: Spain pays the highest price in Europe
item.description: A new study ranks different types of extreme weather by how many lives they claimed in 2025.

item.title: Fancy a taste of the A-list life? These European hotels have celebrity connections
item.description: Many entertainment stars and sports icons have turned their hands to hospitality. From Mediterranean beach retreats to boutique stays, here are the hotels across Europe backed by celebrities.

item.title: Latest news bulletin | November 17th, 2026 – Morning
item.description: Catch up with the most important stories from around Europe and beyond this November 17th, 2026 - latest news, breaking news, World, Business, Entertainment, Politics, Culture, Travel.

item.title: After peace talks snub, Kallas faces reproach and uncertain future
item.description: The glaring exclusion of High Representative Kaja Kallas from the Ukraine-Russia peace talks has raised uncomfortable questions about the relevance of her job. Defiant but isolated, Kallas stands by her words.

item.title: Renault to create 2,000 jobs in France while cutting 1,000 others by 2028
item.description: French car maker Renault announced on Monday plans to create 2,000 jobs by 2028, mostly production roles, while cutting 1,000 mainly administrative staff as it seeks to hold off tough Chinese competition.

item.title: Is personalised medicine the future? EU-backed project to map 100,000 genomes
item.description: A massive European genome bank could pave the way for medicines tailored to each patient's DNA, faster diagnosis of rare diseases and new ways of prevention. Here's how it works.

item.title: US banking app users report widespread outages linked to software bugs
item.description: American users of several major banking apps and online portals reported outages on Monday, according to the monitoring site Downdetector.com, with one institution ruling out a cyberattack as the cause.

item.title: Sánchez and Lula meet in Madrid to strengthen ties amid 'threat of the far right'
item.description: The two leaders are said to have discussed their "bilateral agenda" and reaffirmed their intention to continue strengthening cooperation between Spain and Brazil.

item.title: Europe Tonight: MEPs debate Rwanda deportation scheme announced by five EU countries
item.description: On Euronews' first edition of Europe Tonight, presenter Mared Gwyn Jones led a debate on Europe's latest migration crackdown, after five EU countries announced a partnership with Rwanda to establish deportation hubs for irregular migrants.

item.title: Pope Leo XIV struck in eye by rosary during tour of South America
item.description: The pontiff was able to continue with his schedule and appeared to be uninjured. Leo's tour of South America has also seen him visit Uruguay and Argentina and came just weeks after he underwent lung cancer surgery in Rome.

item.title: Video shows rocket failure that destroys 40 Amazon satellites
item.description: A United Launch Alliance Vulcan rocket suffered an in-flight failure minutes after liftoff from Florida, leaving 40 Amazon internet satellites unable to reach orbit.

item.title: France can no longer support Kyiv 'financially,' Le Pen tells Ukrainian ambassador
item.description: The National Rally party's stance on Ukraine has come under increasing scrutiny over its pledges to withdraw financial support and questions over historical ties to Russia.

item.title: Germany's 'bratwurst tax' sparks backlash as community groups face new VAT rules
item.description: Under new rules, public bodies such as municipalities and towns are to be generally liable for VAT when they engage in commercial activities.

item.title: Qatar Sustainability Week explores ways to cut food waste, track carbon emissions and support wellbeing
item.description: Wasting less and looking after our physical and mental health were among the themes of this year’s Qatar Sustainability Week. Schools, businesses and communities explored how the choices we make when shopping, eating and going about our day can affect both the environment and our wellbeing.

item.title: Italian schools hit by new wave of bomb and poison threats
item.description: Under new security guidelines, Italian schools are no longer automatically evacuated in response to vague, mass-distributed threats, with the decision left to the discretion of law enforcement and security officials.

item.title: Euronews Verify: Is Europe prepared and able to defend against hybrid threats?
item.description: Amid disinformation, cyberattacks and bomb hoaxes, hostile countries and groups are testing Europe's vulnerabilities. Is Europe prepared, or even able, to defend itself?

item.title: Europe Tonight: Five EU states announce Rwanda deportation hubs as EU warns Russia is ‘weaponising winter’
item.description: Five EU nations announce Rwanda deportation hubs by mid-2027. Plus, EU aid chief Hadja Lahbib warns Russia is weaponising winter in Ukraine, Lithuania’s FM Kęstutis Budrys opposes Moscow talks before a ceasefire, and Robert Pattinson is revealed as the next James Bond.
